title: Comparing Machine Learning Forecasting Models Based on Accuracy and Efficiency for Predicting Demand in a Food and Beverage Company
authors: Alunen, Ray Baltazar; Molina, Cyrene Franchesca; Quesada, Raven Francheska; Reyes, Chloe Nicole
tldr: XGBoost achieves best balance of accuracy and efficiency for demand forecasting, outperforming traditional methods by capturing non-linear relationships with external factors.
problem_and_motivation: The Philippine food and beverage industry faces challenges in supply chain efficiency and demand forecasting. Traditional methods fail to capture non-linear relationships and external factors such as holidays, weather, and macroeconomic conditions. Accurate forecasting is critical for minimizing waste, optimizing inventory, and meeting market demands, especially in the alcoholic beverage segment.
approach: Historical sales data from restobar in Quezon City (2021-2024) for alcoholic beverages.
External factors: unemployment rate, temperature, holidays, day of week.
ML algorithms: Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, XGBoost, AdaBoost.
Feature selection using Pearson Correlation Coefficient (threshold ±0.3).
Hyperparameter tuning: Grid Search vs Random Search.
Evaluation metrics: MSE, MAE, RMSE, R², execution time.
findings: num: XGBoost excelled in both accuracy and computational efficiency across products.
num: XGBoost execution time: 9.47s vs Random Forest: 203.67s.
num: Feature selection reduced dimensions but led to slight accuracy reduction.
num: Random Search outperformed Grid Search in accuracy and execution time.
num: Grid Search execution time: 390.43s vs Random Search: 16.91s.
num: All ML models outperformed traditional methods (MLR, Exponential Smoothing).
num: Traditional MLR had R² = 0.39, MAE = 10.44.
num: Exponential Smoothing had R² = 0.07, MAE = 6.83.
Product 1 (Bucket): XGBoost R² = 0.52, Product 2 (Cocktails): RF R² = 0.45.

topics.name: Forecasting Algorithms for Sequential Spending Data
topics.justification: Applies ML algorithms for time-series demand forecasting, though focused on product demand rather than personal spending.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: The study demonstrates that XGBoost achieves the best balance of accuracy (R² = 0.42) and computational efficiency (9.47s) for demand forecasting in F&B. All ML models outperform traditional methods (MLR, Exponential Smoothing) in capturing non-linear relationships. Feature selection using correlation reduces dimensions but introduces slight accuracy trade-offs. Random Search hyperparameter tuning is more efficient than Grid Search (16.91s vs 390.43s). The framework provides a scalable approach for improving supply chain practices in Philippine F&B industry.
